page: Amazon Web Services r8in.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, this instance features 96 virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with two threads per core. The platform provides 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. No discrete GPU hardware is present on this instance.

In terms of networking and data throughput, the r8in.24xlarge is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps for high-throughput inter-node communication. The instance does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes for the operating system and persistent data. As a result, disk I/O performance relies on remote storage configurations while the physical network interface handles both storage and general network traffic.

From a resource density and cost efficiency perspective, the r8in.24xlarge offers a balanced combination of high-clock compute, substantial memory capacity, and large network bandwidth without the cost overhead of local NVMe hardware. This hardware layout fits in-memory databases, large-scale distributed caching, real-time analytics engines, and data processing pipelines.

The instance contains no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote Elastic Block Store volumes for all operational and persistent disk needs. By pairing dense memory capacity with high-frequency processing and broad network throughput, the r8in.24xlarge functions effectively for in-memory databases, distributed caching frameworks, and memory-constrained analytical processing pipelines.
